html:
Charles University in Prague was founded on 7 April 1348 by Charles IV, king of Bohemia and later Holy Roman Emperor, as the first university in central Europe, north of the Alps and east of Paris.

It was modelled on Paris and Bologna and taught arts, law, medicine and theology to students from across the empire, organised in four nations. In 1409 the Decree of Kutná Hora gave the Czech nation three votes, and most German masters left to found the University of Leipzig. Jan Hus was its rector. In 1882 it split into Czech and German universities. The Nazis closed the Czech university in 1939 after student protests. Students marking that date in 1989 started the Velvet Revolution. It is still the largest university in the Czech Republic.
sum: Charles University in Prague was founded on 7 April 1348 by Charles IV, king of Bohemia and later Holy Roman Emperor, as the first university in central Europe, north of the Alps and east of Paris.
